title: Regular-word identification after forgetting the external action
statement:
Use the quasicategory, universe, nerve and coherent-functor conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], monoidal infinity-categories of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], and the planar operad $\mathsf{Chain}_2$ and operator categories of [lem-coef-composable-bimodule-operad-segal]. Let $\mathcal V$ act coherently on $\mathcal M$, let $A$ be an associative unital algebra in $\mathcal V$, and let $Q$ be a coherent left $A$-module in $\mathcal M$; $U_AQ$ denotes its underlying object, forgetting its action.

Specify the action-valued target as follows. Let $\mathsf{BM}$ be the planar operad with colours $v,m,t$ and singleton operation sets exactly for $v^r\to v$, $t^s\to t$, and $v^rmt^s\to m$ ($r,s\geq0$). Its operator category uses the same ordered-block convention as $\mathsf{Chain}_2^\otimes$. Represent the coherent action by its action operad $\pi:\mathcal E^\otimes\to N(\mathsf{BM}^\otimes)$, a cocartesian fibration of nonsymmetric infinity operads: the colour fibers are $\mathcal V,\mathcal M,*$, a list has the product of its colour fibers, and transport along a block is the corresponding iterated tensor or action, ignoring terminal right factors, with the given coherent associativity and units. Thus $\mathcal E_m=\mathcal M$. The map $g:N(\mathsf{Chain}_2^\otimes)\to N(\mathsf{BM}^\otimes)$ sends $a_0,a_1,p$ to $v$, $q$ to $m$ and $a_2$ to $t$, and sends each allowed operation to the unique operation with those colours.

Let $F:N(\mathsf{Chain}_2^\otimes)\to\mathcal E^\otimes$ be an inert-preserving algebra lift over $g$, equipped with the coherent identification $\pi F\simeq g$ (a lift in the relative infinity-category of the cited Segal statement). Its values on $a_0,a_1,p,q,a_2$ are respectively $A,A,A,U_AQ,*$. Its $\mathsf{BM}_{01}$ restriction is coherently the pullback of the algebra $A$ along $c:\mathsf{BM}_{01}\to\mathsf{Ass}_1$, which sends $a_0,p,a_1$ to $a_1$ and each operation to the unique operation of the same arity; its $\mathsf{BM}_{12}$ restriction encodes $Q$ and the terminal right action. These identifications agree on the shared algebra at $a_1$. This is the regularity hypothesis, including both multiplication actions and all coherences.

A block operator from a word $L$ of length $\ell$ to $L'$ of length $\ell'$ is the operator over the opposite of a monotone map $h:[\ell']\to[\ell]$, whose $j$th output is an allowed operation on the consecutive input positions $h(j-1)+1,\ldots,h(j)$. It preserves exterior endpoints if $h(0)=0$ and $h(\ell')=\ell$. Define $R$ to have words $pa_1^nq$ ($n\geq0$) and these endpoint-preserving operators with the input $p$ in the output $p$ block and the input $q$ in the output $q$ block. Define $W$ similarly with words $a_1^kq$ ($k\geq0$), retaining the input $q$ in the final output block. Composition is ordered block substitution. Relabelling $p$ as $a_1$ defines $r:R\to W$.

For either word category $C$, write $b_C=g|_{N(C)}$. Total contraction is the coherent transformation $\beta_C:b_C\to\operatorname{const}(m)$ given at each word by the single $\mathsf{BM}$ operation contracting all its entries. Evaluate $F|_{N(C)}$ by cocartesian transport along the composite $\pi F|_{N(C)}\simeq b_C\xrightarrow{\beta_C}\operatorname{const}(m)$, as in [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport]. Write $Y:N(R)\to\mathcal M$ and $X:N(W)\to\mathcal M$ for the resulting diagrams. There is a coherent equivalence $Y\simeq X\circ N(r)$, with components identifying $A\otimes A^{\otimes n}\otimes U_AQ$ with $A^{\otimes(n+1)}\otimes U_AQ$, compatible with every string of operators in $R$. The diagram $X$ is defined on all of $N(W)$, including the leading-unit arrows $a_1^kq\to a_1^{k+1}q$ over $h:[k+2]\to[k+1]$ with $h(0)=h(1)=0$, $h(j)=j-1$ for $j\geq2$; these have empty first output block and are not in the image of $r$. The comparison is in $\mathcal M$ after forgetting the external left action and asserts no $A$-linearity of a leading-unit insertion. No colimits are assumed.

source.place: Higher Algebra, Construction 4.4.2.7 and the ordered operator convention of Construction 4.2.2.6. Agent-written supporting formulation extracted from the returned proof; read online; WANTED: archived source in literature/. No Stacks tag states the infinity-operadic result.

proof.text: Define an endomorphism $\rho$ of $\mathsf{Chain}_2$ by $\rho(a_0)=\rho(p)=a_1$, fixing $a_1,q,a_2$, and sending every allowed operation to the unique operation of its relabelled type. The $a_0$ operations become $a_1$ operations, $a_0^u p a_1^v\to p$ becomes $a_1^{u+1+v}\to a_1$, and the $q$ and $a_2$ operations are fixed. These are all allowed types, including nullary algebra operations. Substitution and identities are preserved because every relevant operation set is a singleton. On operator categories $\rho$ leaves interval maps unchanged, so preserves inert maps, and $g\circ N(\rho^\otimes)=g$. On $R$ this functor has image in $W$ and is precisely $r$: its first output block contains the first input $a_1$, and its final block contains $q$. Thus $r$ preserves identities and composites. No inverse of $r$ is asserted.

source.place: Construction 4.2.2.6; ordered operations of the cited planar Segal lemma; elementary relabelling.

proof.text: Put $F'=F\circ N(\rho^\otimes)$, with its induced coherent base identification over $g$. On $\mathsf{BM}_{12}$, $F'=F$ since $\rho$ is the identity there. On $\mathsf{BM}_{01}$, $\rho$ factors as $c$ followed by $\mathsf{Ass}_1\hookrightarrow\mathsf{Chain}_2$; hence $F'$ restricts to $A\circ c$. The regularity hypothesis supplies a coherent equivalence from $F|_{\mathsf{BM}_{01}}$ to this restriction, agreeing with the identity on the shared $A$. Together with the identity on $\mathsf{BM}_{12}$ it is an equivalence between the two restriction triples, including their gluing and base identifications. Apply the relative Segal restriction equivalence over the fixed $g$, with target $\mathcal E^\otimes\to N(\mathsf{BM}^\otimes)$. A quasi-inverse to that equivalence carries this equivalence of triples to an equivalence $\epsilon:F\simeq F'$ of algebra lifts over $g$. In particular its inverse and the two inverse homotopies are coherent transformations over $g$. This uses regularity as an identification of entire operadic lifts, rather than only equality of multiplication maps.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.1.11 and the relative algebra-lift formulation of the cited node; agent specialization by rho.

proof.text: Let $K=N(R)$, $D=F|_K$ and $D'=F|_{N(W)}\circ N(r)$. Restriction of $\epsilon$ gives $e:D\simeq D'$ over the common base $b=b_R=b_W\circ N(r)$. Write $\delta:\pi D\simeq b$ and $\delta':\pi D'\simeq b$ for the base identifications; being over $b$ includes the homotopy $\delta'\circ\pi e\simeq\delta$. Total contractions are natural: substituting any endpoint-preserving operator into the final contraction gives the unique operation on the entire input word. Relabelling does not change its image in $\mathsf{BM}$, so $\beta_R=\beta_W\circ N(r)$. Consequently, for $G=\operatorname{const}(m)$ and $\gamma=\beta_R\delta$, $\gamma'=\beta_R\delta'$, the equivalence $e$ includes the homotopy $\gamma'\circ\pi e\simeq\gamma$. All these are transformations of whole $K$-diagrams by restriction of the corresponding simplicial maps.

source.place: Construction 4.4.2.7, total-contraction transformation; elementary restriction of the relative Segal comparison.

proof.text: Apply pointwise cocartesian transport to $\pi$, first with $N(W)$ and its total-contraction transformation, then with $K$ and $\gamma$. The categories $R,W$ are small (finite words and finite monotone maps), and $\pi$ has quasicategorical source and target and cocartesian lifts by the action-target hypothesis. We obtain $\lambda_W:F|_{N(W)}\to X$ and $\lambda:D\to Y$ with cocartesian vertex components and target over $m$. The constant-base fibers are respectively $\operatorname{Fun}(N(W),\mathcal M)$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal M)$. The product-of-colour-fibers description and the specified total-contraction transport identify their values as $X(a_1^kq)\simeq A^{\otimes k}\otimes U_AQ$ and $Y(pa_1^nq)\simeq A\otimes A^{\otimes n}\otimes U_AQ$. Iterated tensor/action is interpreted using its given associativity and unit equivalences, as in the monoidal Segal convention; $A^{\otimes0}$ contributes the unit.

source.place: Construction 4.4.2.7; action-valued Example 4.4.2.12 and the stated tensor convention.

proof.text: Precompose $\lambda_W$ with $N(r)$ and write $Z=X\circ N(r)$, $\lambda':D'\to Z$. Its base is $\gamma'$ by Step 3. Every vertex component remains a $\pi$-cocartesian edge. The if direction of the pointwise criterion, now applied with index $K$, therefore makes $\lambda'$ a cocartesian transport of $D'$ along $\gamma'$ in the same functor-category fibration as $\lambda$. This verifies restriction of transport using the criterion's stated hypothesis; it does not infer a comparison merely from matching object values.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.2.1, cocartesian dual; pointwise criterion with index N(R).

proof.text: Work in the constant-base fiber $\mathcal F_G=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal M)$. The composite $\lambda'e:D\to Z$, with the base homotopy of Step 3, is a point of the homotopy fiber over $\gamma$ in the transport lemma's mapping-space formula. Its inverse image gives $u:Y\to Z$ with $u\lambda\simeq\lambda'e$. Apply the same formula to $\lambda'$ and $\lambda e^{-1}$, using the inverse base homotopy, to obtain $v:Z\to Y$ with $v\lambda'\simeq\lambda e^{-1}$. Thus $(vu)\lambda\simeq v\lambda'e\simeq\lambda e^{-1}e\simeq\lambda$ in the homotopy fiber over $\gamma$; the specified base homotopies agree because $e^{-1}e\simeq1_D$ is an inverse homotopy over $b$. The mapping-space equivalence for $H=Y$ pulls this homotopy back to $vu\simeq1_Y$. Similarly, using the formula for $\lambda'$ with $H=Z$ gives $uv\simeq1_Z$. Naturality in $H$ and the composition/precomposition compatibility stated in the transport lemma justify these compositions in the mapping fibers. These two inverse homotopies prove $Y\simeq Z$ inside $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal M)$. The inverse used here is the inverse of $e$, supplied by Step 2, not an inverse relabelling functor.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.2 and Proposition 2.4.1.7, cocartesian duals; mapping-space fiber formula in the functor category.

proof.text: An edge of $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal M)$ is a simplicial map $K\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal M$; hence the equivalence in Step 6 restricts to a coherent comparison on each simplex of $K$, namely every string of operators of $R$, and its faces and degeneracies agree by restriction. The inverse homotopies are simplices of the same functor category, so retain those compatibilities as well. At a word $pa_1^nq$, the restriction equivalence of Step 2 identifies the $p$ factor with the first $a_1$ factor using the specified regular $A\circ c$, and fixes the remaining $A$ factors and $Q$. Its transported component is therefore the tensor identification of Step 4. The transport lemma's composition clause identifies successive tensor/action transports with total contraction, compatibly with the precomposition maps that defined $u,v$; thus the tensor interpretation has the same coherent comparison on operator strings. No separate choice of maps on strings is being assembled.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.2.1 and Proposition 2.4.1.7, cocartesian duals; unpacking the coherent functor-category equivalence.

proof.text: The construction of $X$ in Step 4 uses all of $N(W)$. The displayed leading-unit map is an allowed $W$-operator: $h$ is monotone with both exterior endpoints fixed, the first output block is empty, the later algebra blocks are singletons, and the last block contains $q$. In the image of $r$, the first output block contains the relabelled input $p$, so is nonempty; therefore this operator is outside that image (also for $k=0$, when its source is $q$). All our transports land in $\mathcal E_m=\mathcal M$, so the comparison has exactly the asserted underlying target and makes no claim about an external left action.

source.place: Construction 4.2.2.6, endpoint and empty-block check; Construction 4.4.2.7, underlying output fiber.

proof_origin.place: Repair via the relative Segal equivalence (Proposition 4.4.1.11) applied to rho, followed by total contraction (Construction 4.4.2.7) and the functor-category mapping-space transport formula (HTT 3.1.2.1, 2.4.4.2, 2.4.1.7, duals). Sources read online; no archived copies in literature/.
